fichas.title: CHP and block heating and power systems
fichas.summary: Combined heat and power (CHP) produces electricity and useful heat simultaneously. Block heating and power systems are sized around a building’s electricity or heating demand, typically supplying base heat and feeding excess electricity into the grid, with supplementary heating for peak demand. The page describes system sizes, required floor area, and installation provisions for air supply, exhaust, and sound insulation.
uses: Feed excess electricity into the grid
Provide heating for buildings or groups of buildings

fichas.title: Fuel cells
fichas.summary: Fuel cells generate electricity and heat through a reverse-electrolysis process involving anode, cathode, and electrolyte. Their direct-current output is converted to alternating current by an inverter, while waste heat can serve space heating through a cooling circuit. The page outlines fuel-cell types by electrolyte and operating temperature and notes that system sizing can follow electricity or heating demand, with supplementary capacity for peak loads.
uses: Supply space heating using waste heat
Cover base electricity or heating demand
Drive absorption refrigeration using excess summer heat
